fullPassage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals.

questions.passage: Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences (A)[enable / prevent] them to help others. They are good (B)[listeners / speakers] and view all experiences as (C)[opportunities / obstacles] to understand others' hardships.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 고통스러운 경험이 다른 사람을 도울 수 있게 해 준다. 좋은 경청자. 경험을 기회로 본다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① enable — listeners — opportunities
❌ ② prevent — listeners — obstacles
❌ ③ enable — speakers — obstacles
❌ ④ prevent — speakers — opportunities
✅ (A) enable: '가능하게 하다'. prevent(막다)는 도움 맥락과 반대. ✅ (B) listeners: '경청자'. speakers(연설자)는 원문과 다름. ✅ (C) opportunities: '기회'. obstacles(장애물)는 반대 의미.
det.tip: enable(가능하게 하다) ↔ prevent(막다). opportunities(기회) ↔ obstacles(장애물).

questions.passage: People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who (A)[overcome / avoid] suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can (B)[evolve / regress] into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and (C)[learn / suffer] from them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 고통을 극복하는 사람들이 치유자가 된다. 상처 입은 리더로 발전한다. 상처로부터 배운다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① overcome — evolve — learn
❌ ② avoid — evolve — suffer
❌ ③ overcome — regress — suffer
❌ ④ avoid — regress — learn
✅ (A) overcome: '극복하다'. avoid(피하다)는 맥락 불일치. ✅ (B) evolve: '발전하다'. regress(퇴보하다)는 반대. ✅ (C) learn: '배우다'. suffer(고통받다)는 이미 겪은 것.
det.tip: overcome(극복하다) ↔ avoid(피하다). evolve(발전하다) ↔ regress(퇴보하다).

questions.passage: In fact, wounds in leadership would be (A)[transformative / destructive] because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at (B)[peace / war]. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to (C)[embrace / reject] the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 상처는 변화를 가져오는 것. 리더는 더 평화로워진다. 치유 과정을 포용하는 능력.
det.analysis:
✅ ① transformative — peace — embrace
❌ ② destructive — peace — reject
❌ ③ transformative — war — reject
❌ ④ destructive — war — embrace
✅ (A) transformative: '변화를 가져오는'. destructive(파괴적인)는 긍정적 맥락과 반대. ✅ (B) peace: '평화'. war(전쟁)는 맥락 불일치. ✅ (C) embrace: '포용하다'. reject(거부하다)는 치유 과정과 반대.
det.tip: transformative(변화를 가져오는) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). embrace(포용) ↔ reject(거부).

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is ①<u>credited</u> with coining the term "a wounded healer." Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences ②<u>enable</u> them to help others. They are good ③<u>listeners</u> and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' ④<u>pleasures</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람들의 어려움(hardships)을 이해한다. 즐거움(pleasures)이 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①credited(인정받는): 용어를 만든 것으로 인정받음. ✅ ②enable(가능하게 하다): 도움을 가능케 함. ✅ ③listeners(경청자): 좋은 경청자. ❌ ④pleasures(즐거움): 원문은 hardships(어려움). 고통의 맥락에서 즐거움은 부적절.
det.tip: hardships(어려움, 고난) ↔ pleasures(즐거움, 기쁨). 상처 입은 치유자가 이해하는 것은 고난.

questions.passage: People who go through ①<u>suffering</u> do not always become healers. It is those who ②<u>overcome</u> suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and ③<u>learn</u> from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be ④<u>insignificant</u> because they lead to deeper self knowledge.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 리더십에서 상처는 변화를 가져올 것이다. 하찮은(insignificant) 것이 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①suffering(고통): 고통을 겪는 사람들. ✅ ②overcome(극복하다): 고통을 극복. ✅ ③learn(배우다): 상처로부터 배움. ❌ ④insignificant(하찮은): 원문은 transformative(변화를 가져오는). 더 깊은 지식으로 이어지므로 하찮은 것과 반대.
det.tip: transformative(변화를 가져오는) ↔ insignificant(하찮은). 상처가 리더십에 긍정적 변화를 가져옴.

questions.passage: Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at ①<u>peace</u>. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to ②<u>embrace</u> the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: ③<u>accepting</u> different perspectives and focusing on personal ④<u>decline</u> while pursuing their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자기 발전(development)에 집중한다. 쇠퇴(decline)가 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①peace(평화): 더 평화로워짐. ✅ ②embrace(포용하다): 치유 과정 포용. ✅ ③accepting(받아들이는): 다른 관점 수용. ❌ ④decline(쇠퇴): 원문은 development(발전). 목표 추구 중 개인 발전에 집중하는 맥락.
det.tip: development(발전, 성장) ↔ decline(쇠퇴, 감소). personal development = 자기 계발.

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good __________ and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 경청자(listeners)이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① leaders
❌ ② fighters
✅ ③ listeners
❌ ④ healers
✅ listeners(경청자): 타인의 이야기를 잘 듣는 사람. ❌ leaders(리더): 이후에 등장하는 개념. ❌ fighters(투사): 문맥 불일치. ❌ healers(치유자): 이미 wounded healers로 설명됨.
det.tip: listener(경청자) = 남의 말을 잘 듣는 사람. good listener = 좋은 경청자.

questions.passage: Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be __________ because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 상처는 변화를 가져올 것이다. 더 깊은 자기 지식, 더 강한 관계, 더 큰 리더십 기술로 이어지기 때문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① transformative
❌ ② destructive
❌ ③ temporary
❌ ④ irrelevant
✅ transformative(변화를 가져오는): 긍정적 변화(지식, 관계, 기술)로 이어짐. ❌ destructive(파괴적인): 긍정적 결과와 반대. ❌ temporary(일시적인): 영속적 변화. ❌ irrelevant(무관한): 리더십에 직접 영향.
det.tip: transformative = 변화를 가져오는. transform(변환하다) + -ive(형용사 접미사).

questions.passage: People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different __________ and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 관점(perspectives)을 받아들이고 자기 계발에 집중한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① challenges
❌ ② emotions
✅ ③ wounds
❌ ④ perspectives
✅ perspectives(관점): 치유 과정에서 다른 관점을 수용. ❌ challenges(도전): 관점과 다른 개념. ❌ emotions(감정): accepting과 결합 가능하나 원문 아님. ❌ wounds(상처): 이미 상위 개념으로 사용됨.
det.tip: perspective = 관점, 시각. different perspectives = 다른 관점/시각들. accept different perspectives = 다양한 관점을 수용하다.

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with <u>coining</u> the term "a wounded healer."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 coining과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: '상처 입은 치유자'라는 용어를 만든 것.
det.analysis:
❌ ① copying
✅ ② creating
❌ ③ explaining
❌ ④ borrowing
✅ creating(만들다): coining과 가장 가까운 의미. ❌ copying(복사): 새로 만드는 것이 아님. ❌ explaining(설명): 만드는 것과 다름. ❌ borrowing(빌리다): 차용이 아닌 창조.
det.tip: coin a term = 용어를 만들다/주조하다. coin은 '동전을 주조하다'에서 '새 말을 만들다'로 확장.

questions.passage: It is those who <u>overcome</u> suffering who can become wounded healers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 overcome과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 고통을 극복하는 사람들이 치유자가 된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conquer
❌ ② avoid
❌ ③ create
❌ ④ endure
✅ conquer(정복하다, 이기다): overcome과 동의어. ❌ avoid(피하다): 극복이 아닌 회피. ❌ create(만들다): 고통을 만드는 것 아님. ❌ endure(견디다): 극복과 견디기는 다름.
det.tip: overcome = conquer = 극복하다, 이겨내다. ↔ submit to, yield to(굴복하다).

questions.passage: In fact, wounds in leadership would be <u>transformative</u> because they lead to deeper self knowledge.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 transformative와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 상처는 변화를 가져오는 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① harmful
❌ ② temporary
✅ ③ revolutionary
❌ ④ insignificant
✅ revolutionary(혁명적인, 획기적인): transformative와 가장 가까운 의미. ❌ harmful(해로운): 부정적 의미. ❌ temporary(일시적인): 영구적 변화. ❌ insignificant(하찮은): 중요한 변화와 반대.
det.tip: transformative = revolutionary = 변화를 가져오는, 획기적인. 근본적 변화를 이끄는.

questions.passage: They are good listeners and view all experiences as <u>opportunities</u> to understand others' hardships.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 opportunities와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 경험을 기회로 본다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacles
❌ ② chances
❌ ③ occasions
❌ ④ moments
✅ obstacles(장애물): opportunities의 반의어. ❌ chances(기회): 동의어. ❌ occasions(경우): 유사. ❌ moments(순간): 다른 범주.
det.tip: opportunities(기회) ↔ obstacles(장애물). chance = opportunity(동의어).

questions.passage: Their leadership style is characterized by the ability to <u>embrace</u> the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 embrace와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 치유 과정을 포용하는 능력.
det.analysis:
❌ ① accept
❌ ② welcome
✅ ③ adopt
❌ ④ reject
✅ reject(거부하다): embrace의 정확한 반의어. ❌ accept(받아들이다): 동의어. ❌ welcome(환영하다): 동의어. ❌ adopt(채택하다): 유사.
det.tip: embrace(포용하다) ↔ reject(거부하다). accept = welcome = embrace(동의어). 오답 3개가 동의어.

questions.passage:
(A) Leaders who have <u>dealt</u> with their wounds find themselves more at peace.

(B) The company <u>dealt</u> in electronic products and had branches across the country.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 dealt의 의미로 가장 적절한 것을 (A), (B)에서 각각 고르면?

det.korean: (A) 상처를 처리한(극복한) 리더. (B) 전자 제품을 거래한 회사.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 거래하다 — (B) 처리하다
❌ ② (A) 분배하다 — (B) 거래하다
✅ ③ (A) 처리하다 — (B) 거래하다
❌ ④ (A) 처리하다 — (B) 분배하다
✅ (A) 처리하다: deal with = 처리하다, 다루다. (B) 거래하다: deal in = ~을 거래하다. ❌ (A)를 거래하다: 상처와 거래 불가. ❌ (B)를 분배하다: deal in은 거래 의미.
det.tip: deal with = ~을 처리하다, 다루다. deal in = ~을 거래하다. 전치사에 따라 의미 변화.

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer.
questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"causing a major change or improvement in something"

det.korean: 무언가에 큰 변화나 개선을 일으키는 = 변화를 가져오는(transformative).
det.analysis:
❌ ① destructive
❌ ② temporary
✅ ③ insignificant
❌ ④ transformative
✅ transformative: 큰 변화/개선을 일으키는. ❌ destructive(파괴적인): 변화가 아닌 파괴. ❌ temporary(일시적인): 큰 변화와 무관. ❌ insignificant(하찮은): 반대.
det.tip: transformative = 변혁적인, 변화를 가져오는. transform(변형하다) + -ative.

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them __________ (help) others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 고통스러운 경험이 다른 사람을 도울 수 있게 해 준다.
det.analysis: enable + O + to V 구문. enable them to help = 그들이 돕는 것을 가능하게 하다.
det.tip: enable + 목적어 + to V = ~가 ...할 수 있게 하다. help → to help.

questions.passage: Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Their leadership style is __________ (characterize) by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그들의 리더십 유형은 치유 과정을 포용할 수 있는 능력이 특징이다.
det.analysis: 수동태 is + p.p. 구조. characterize → characterized. is characterized by = ~이 특징이다.
det.tip: be characterized by = ~이 특징이다. characterize(특징짓다)의 수동태.

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. This implies that __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: personal suffering can be a foundation for helping others
only professional doctors can become healers
healing others requires avoiding one's own pain
everyone who suffers automatically becomes a healer

det.korean: 다시 말해, 개인적 고통이 타인을 돕는 기반이 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① only professional doctors can become healers
✅ ② personal suffering can be a foundation for helping others
❌ ③ healing others requires avoiding one's own pain
❌ ④ everyone who suffers automatically becomes a healer
✅ 고통이 도움의 기반: wounded(상처) → healer(치유자)의 핵심 논리. ❌ 전문 의사만: 제한 없음. ❌ 자신의 고통 회피: 반대로 상처를 경험해야 함. ❌ 모든 고통 → 자동 치유자: 'not always' 명시.
det.tip: In other words(다시 말해): 앞 내용의 핵심 재진술. '상처를 받아야 치유자가 된다'의 요약.

questions.passage: It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals. This implies that __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: effective leaders should never reveal their weaknesses
overcoming personal struggles can make a leader more effective
personal wounds are irrelevant to leadership ability
the best leaders are those who have never experienced hardship

det.korean: 개인적 어려움을 극복하면 더 효과적인 리더가 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① effective leaders should never reveal their weaknesses
❌ ② personal wounds are irrelevant to leadership ability
✅ ③ overcoming personal struggles can make a leader more effecti
❌ ④ the best leaders are those who have never experienced hardsh
✅ 어려움 극복 → 효과적 리더: 상처가 transformative, deeper knowledge, peace로 이어짐. ❌ 약점 숨기기: embrace 맥락과 반대. ❌ 상처 무관: 반대로 직접적 관련. ❌ 고난 없는 리더: 상처 경험이 핵심.
det.tip: This suggests that = 이것은 ~을 시사한다. 글의 논지를 추론하는 문제.
